metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Enumerate the FULL poll status vocabulary in the plan/contract — add 'attaching' (follower before leader index write; keep polling) and 'unknown' (unrecognised job_id) alongside running/passed/failed/stale-running, and state the agent's required action for each so an MCP-only client branches correctly.
evidence: Plan enumerates only: '{run_id,status:'running'}' and 'poll transitions running→passed/failed' and '"stale-running" status read' — never 'attaching' or 'unknown'.

gate_runs.gate_run_status docstring: "status is running / passed / failed / stale-running / attaching / unknown" and returns {"status": "attaching"} when _inflight.is_job_active(job_id) but no index record, else {"status": "unknown"}.

_mcp_reads.gate_status docstring documents 'attaching' ('a duplicate start attached to an in-flight run whose index record has not landed yet (keep polling)') and 'unknown' ('the job_id is unrecognised') — states the plan never names.

ABSENCE rationale: an MCP-only polling agent (the exact consumer the plan targets under 'Mandated path' / AC #4 portability) branches on this enum; a value it has never been told about is an undefined-vocabulary gap the executor needs.
findings.finding: The plan defines the async poll surface (review_plan_start/verify_completion_start + gate_status/plan_review_status/verify_completion_status) as the agent-consumed contract but under-specifies its status enum: it names only running/passed/failed/stale-running, while the surface a polling agent actually observes also emits 'attaching' (a de-dup follower whose leader index record has not landed yet — semantics: keep polling) and 'unknown' (unrecognised job_id). An agent coded to the plan's four documented states has no defined handling for these two, and could mis-treat the non-terminal 'attaching' as a terminal/missing result.
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 2; Acceptance criteria AC #1 ('the caller receives either the verdict or a pollable in-progress signal/handle')
scenarios: A follower *_start attaches and the agent polls gate_status before the leader writes its index — receives status='attaching' the plan never defined, and may abort or mis-classify as done.
An agent polls a stale/typo'd job_id and receives 'unknown', with no plan-defined semantics for whether to retry the start or escalate.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Phase-2 contract and AC #1, define the complete gate_status enum: running | passed | failed | stale-running | attaching | unknown, with per-value agent guidance ('attaching'/'running'/'stale-running' ⇒ keep polling and consult durable; 'passed'/'failed' ⇒ terminal; 'unknown' ⇒ job_id not found, do not retry-attach). Cross-reference that plan_review_status/verify_completion_status expose the separate durable verdict vocabulary (certified/unsigned/stale-*).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the fresh-container/durable-verdict test exercise the real git-backed event-log persist+read round-trip (write via one run instance, read via a freshly-constructed registry/reader over the same store), not an in-memory stub, so the durability claim is validated on the production path.
evidence: 'a fresh registry (simulated new container) still resolves the durable verdict'

Tests are described as monkeypatching rebar.llm.review_plan/verify_completion with a blocking fake; it is not stated whether the fresh-container test hits the real .rebar event log persistence or a stub.
findings.finding: The durability claim (verdict survives a blue-green flip via the git-backed event log) is load-bearing, but the described test 'a fresh registry (simulated new container) still resolves the durable verdict' is not stated to exercise the REAL git-backed event-log round-trip — if it reads a fake/in-memory verdict it is proxy-validation of the very persistence mechanism AC #4 (portability across MCP-only, no-checkout clients) depends on.
scenarios: The suite goes green on the durability test while the real event-log read/write path (the thing that lets an MCP-only client observe completion after a flip) is never exercised end-to-end, letting a broken durable-verdict path close green.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the concurrency scope of the in-process singleflight dedup: either establish that concurrent same-ticket MCP requests are serialized to one worker/process (so AC #2 holds), or explicitly scope AC #2 to single-process concurrency and acknowledge the bounded multi-process double-billing window (and how it is bounded/accepted).
evidence: Plan: 'a new leaf module src/rebar/_mcp_inflight.py — an in-process singleflight registry'
Plan: 'Durability across a blue-green flip comes from the git-backed verdict … not from in-process state (stateless_http=True by design)'
AC #2: 'A re-invocation while a review for the same ticket+basis is in flight attaches to that run and does NOT start a second billable LLM review'

ABSENCE: the plan does not state whether concurrent MCP requests for one ticket are serialized to a single worker/process, so the in-process guarantee's scope vs. a stateless_http multi-process deployment is unaddressed
findings.finding: Phase 1's anti-double-billing guarantee (AC #2) rests on an IN-PROCESS singleflight registry, but the plan also states the server is stateless_http=True; under a multi-worker/multi-process HTTP deployment two concurrent same-key calls could land on different processes and each launch a billable LLM run, so AC #2's 'does NOT start a second billable run' is only guaranteed within a single process. The plan reconciles verdict DURABILITY across a flip via git but never scopes the dedup guarantee to single-process concurrency nor argues the residual multi-process double-billing window away (e.g. that a client's requests pin to one worker, or that the deployment is single-process).
scenarios: A hosted MCP server runs multiple worker processes; a client's -32001 retry is dispatched to a different worker than the in-flight leader, so the retry's registry lookup misses and a second billable LLM pass starts — the exact waste AC #2 promises to prevent
Blue-green flip where old and new fleet briefly co-serve and a retry hits the new process

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify that Phase 1 resolves only AC#2 (no second billable run) and that AC#1 (no opaque timeout / pollable handle) is resolved by Phase 2, since a same-key waiter still blocks past the 60s client timeout.
evidence: Phase 1: 'a second concurrent caller for the same key awaits the SAME computation and shares its verdict'
Root cause: 'client-side SDK timeout (DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC=60000, resetTimeoutOnProgress=false)'
AC#1 and AC#2 both shown as [x]
findings.finding: Phase 1 (singleflight) alone does NOT satisfy AC#1 for either caller: a second same-key caller 'awaits the SAME computation' and therefore still blocks past the client SDK's 60s DEFAULT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MSEC, so it too receives -32001 even though it attached to the in-flight run. The plan lands Phase 1 FIRST as the 'immediate cost-stop' but AC#1 ('no opaque transport timeout ... receives either the verdict or a pollable handle') is only met once Phase 2 ships. Both ACs are pre-marked [x].
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 1 vs AC #1; Acceptance criteria
scenarios: Between Phase 1 landing and Phase 2 landing, an operator sees dedup stop double-billing but the first (and attached second) caller STILL gets -32001 — the caller-experience half of the fix is not yet present.
findings.suggested_fix: Scope AC#1 to Phase 2, or note explicitly that Phase 1's waiter still times out client-side (only the server-side run is deduped) so no reader assumes dedup ends the -32001 experience.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix a single term for the gate handle (recommend `job_id` throughout, mirroring `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>`) and use it consistently in the Expected section, output models, and docs.
evidence: Expected: 'a durable job handle / in-progress token'
Phase 2: '{job_id,…,status:running}' and '.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>'
Durability: 'a run_finished marker'
findings.finding: Terminology drift between the two durable subsystems: Phase 2 introduces 'job_id' / '.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>' while the reused pattern uses 'run_id' / '.rebar/workflow_runs/' and 'run_finished' marker. The plan mixes 'job handle', 'in-progress token', 'run_id', and 'job_id' for the gate handle without fixing one term.
scenarios: Docstrings/docs and the output model could name the field inconsistently (job_id vs run_id vs handle), confusing MCP-only clients that must parse it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the retire/cleanup path (or bounded retention / GC) for .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index files, matching how .rebar/workflow_runs entries are aged out.
evidence: 'A git-ignored .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index (mirroring .rebar/workflow_runs/) maps job_id->(ticket,gate,basis).'
Purge-on-completion/max-age sweep is described only for the in-process singleflight registry, not for the gate_runs index; no expiry or GC is stated for the index files.
findings.finding: Phase 2 introduces a git-ignored .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index (shared on-disk state), but the plan states no RETIRE/cleanup path for these per-job index files — only the in-process registry gets 'purge-on-completion + max-age sweep'. The on-disk index therefore accumulates one file per gate run indefinitely.
scenarios: A long-lived MCP server or busy repo accumulates unbounded .rebar/gate_runs/ entries; nothing reaps completed job_id files, mirroring an unretired workflow_runs-style leak.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the chosen poll-tool shape as a default (e.g. 'deliver a single generic `gate_status`; add `verify_completion_status` only if the output model diverges') rather than leaving 'X or Y' to the executor.
evidence: 'Poll via the existing plan_review_status plus a new verify_completion_status (or a single generic gate_status)'
'optional src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py'
findings.finding: Phase 1's singleflight leaves the poll/handle contract to a deferred choice: 'verify_completion_status (or a single generic gate_status)' and 'optional src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py' defer a real design decision to the executor rather than stating which is delivered.
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 2; Fix plan — file impact
scenarios: Executor must pick between two poll-tool shapes without a stated default, risking an interface that later docs/AGENTS.md guidance contradicts.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one: default to a single generic `gate_status(job_id)` returning `{status, verdict?}`, and make `gate_runs.py` non-optional if the job_id→(ticket,gate,basis) index is needed by both start tools.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify singleflight error semantics: purge the key immediately on failure (not just on success) so the next call retries fresh, and decide whether waiters share the leader's error or re-attempt.
evidence: 'a second concurrent caller for the same key awaits the SAME computation and shares its verdict'
'Purge-on-completion (correctness needs no TTL)'
ABSENCE: no statement of what happens to waiters when the shared computation raises, nor whether failed results are purged immediately vs cached
findings.finding: The plan does not specify singleflight ERROR-propagation semantics. Golang singleflight shares the leader's result INCLUDING its error to all waiters — if the leader's LLM/gate call raises (transient Bedrock/Anthropic error), every attached waiter fails with the same error rather than independently retrying, potentially amplifying a single transient failure into N failed callers, or (if errors are cached) poisoning subsequent callers until purge.
scenarios: Leader's Bedrock call hits a rate-limit/500; all concurrently-attached callers receive the same failure instead of one retrying.
A failed run left in the registry could serve a stale error to a later caller if purge only runs on success.
findings.suggested_fix: State: 'a raised computation purges the key in the same finally as success; waiters observe the leader's exception (no independent retry mid-flight) but the NEXT invocation re-runs since the key is gone.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the atomic register-or-attach primitive (lock/CAS around the registry lookup+insert) that makes singleflight race-free, and add a test that stresses truly-concurrent same-key inserts to prove exactly one run launches.
evidence: 'an in-process singleflight registry (golang singleflight semantics: a second concurrent caller for the same key awaits the SAME computation and shares its verdict)'

The plan states the desired outcome but not the concurrency primitive guaranteeing atomic insert; the sync bodies are wrapped via 'async def + anyio.to_thread', so concurrent callers can race the lookup.
findings.finding: The singleflight registry's own insert is a check-then-act (look up key -> if absent, register + start computation). The plan cites 'golang singleflight semantics' but never states the atomic mechanism (lock/CAS) that makes the register-or-attach step atomic, so two truly-concurrent same-key callers could both miss the registry and each start a billable run — the exact cost defect the plan targets.
scenarios: Two agents (or one agent's retry) invoke review_plan for the same ticket+basis within the same event-loop tick / before the first registers; both miss the registry and launch two Bedrock/Anthropic runs — AC #2's no-second-run guarantee is violated under real concurrency.
findings.suggested_fix: Hold a threading.Lock across the registry get-or-create so the first caller atomically installs the in-flight entry before releasing; document this in _mcp_inflight.py and assert single-invocation under N concurrent threads.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State, with an explicit disposition word, what gate_status surfaces when the async gate job errors mid-run vs is killed by a blue-green flip (e.g. stale-running is retryable/re-invokable; a signed BLOCK is fatal), and that re-invocation of a stale-running job attaches rather than double-bills.
evidence: 'A flip that kills an in-flight run costs at most one re-run; a run_finished marker in a finally + a stale-running status read bound the worst case.'
'poll transitions running->passed/failed' — covers verdict outcomes but not a job that errors (exception) mid-run; no explicit retryable/fatal disposition word for that arm.
findings.finding: The plan alters timeout/failure semantics for a long op and adds a fallback arm (sync tools 'stay as a now-dedup-protected fallback'; a blue-green flip that kills an in-flight run) but never states, using explicit disposition words, what the poll surfaces when the async gate JOB ITSELF errors mid-run (LLM pass raises) versus is killed by a flip. 'stale-running' and 'at most one re-run' imply retryable, but the disposition a caller must treat a run-error result as is not made explicit.
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 2 durability / stale-running paragraph
scenarios: An MCP-only agent polls gate_status, sees a terminal-error or stale-running state after a flip, and cannot tell whether to safely re-invoke (retryable) or must not (fatal) — risking either a stuck ticket or a masked paid re-run.
